description:
The ecclesiastical collection of Naousa on Paros preserves material from the island’s religious artistic heritage. Local museum documentation identifies a Byzantine icon collection associated with Agios Athanasios.

Icons and painted church furnishings connect devotional subjects with traditional craftsmanship. A documented seventeenth-century altarscreen door illustrates how religious imagery formed part of the setting of worship.

description:
The ecclesiastical museum of the Metropolis of Paronaxia is located beside the cathedral in Naxos town. Its collections document the religious heritage of the island’s churches and monasteries.

Historic icons, episcopal vestments, pectoral ornaments and pastoral staffs represent different forms of sacred art. Important ecclesiastical manuscripts also connect the collection with the history of the local church and island society.

description:
The ecclesiastical museum at Chalki on Naxos is associated with the church of Panagia Protothronos. Its collections preserve sacred art and furnishings from the island’s Christian heritage.

Portable icons, detached medieval wall paintings, religious vessels and carved marble elements connect painting with church craftsmanship. The material offers context for the long artistic history of Chalki and surrounding religious sites.

description:
The Historical and Ethnological Museum of the Greeks of Cappadocia in Nea Karvali preserves the history and traditions of Cappadocian Greek communities. Its collections connect the settlement with the heritage brought by refugees.

Heirlooms, everyday objects, religious material and historical documents support this account. The museum is also connected with the local cultural centre and the continuation of Cappadocian customs in the community.

description:
The Museum of Modern Greek Culture in Athens collects and studies material relating to the country’s more recent cultural history. Its collections draw on mainland Greece, the islands and other regions connected with Greek communities.

Objects dating from the seventeenth to twentieth centuries document material traditions and everyday life. A photographic archive adds records of architecture, crafts and other aspects of cultural heritage gathered through research.

description:
The collection of the Taxiarch church in Sagri on Naxos preserves religious painting associated with the village. A documented portable icon of Saint Tryphon provides an example of its devotional imagery.

The wooden icon dates to the first half of the nineteenth century and depicts the saint against a dark green background. Such material connects the collection with local traditions of sacred painting.
